root_cause: BaseScript::swapData/releaseData assumed that GCStructPtr::set() barriers were sufficient for updating the data_ pointer, which was true when PrivateScriptData was a plain heap allocation. Once Bug 2002790 made data_ a BufferAllocator-managed (nursery-capable) allocation, the pointer itself became a GC edge requiring its own trace/write barrier (via TraceBufferEdge), which was not added at the same time, leaving a gap between allocation-strategy change and barrier coverage.
findings: BaseScript::swapData() updates the BaseScript::data_ pointer (a BufferAllocator-managed allocation holding PrivateScriptData) using only `data_.set(zone(), other)`. That GCStructPtr::set() call only triggers a write barrier for the *contents* pointed to by data_ (i.e. the GC things referenced from inside PrivateScriptData), but it performs no write/read barrier for the buffer allocation pointer it
